display_name: Spawn MCP bridge subprocess (macOS coding-agent session plugin)
description: Returns promptly with data.job_id and data.status=queued after persisting the request. The existing platform job worker performs the operation; retrieve its completed result or error with service_interface::job_service::get_job using this exact job_id. A queue receipt does not assert that the operation succeeded. The dispatched plugin action queues bridge creation. Its completed result retains status, agent_instance_id, solet_name, pid, started_at and message. The separate Python CodingAgentSessionServiceInterface.spawn_bridge method still returns BridgeSpawnResult synchronously for internal callers such as the iTerm2 plugin; this dispatch receipt does not change that typed interface.
embedding_description: Queue macOS MCP bridge subprocess creation and return job_id with queued status. Read job_service.get_job for the prior bridge status, pid and audit fields. The separate Python coding-agent session service method still returns its typed BridgeSpawnResult synchronously for internal callers.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch: {job_id, status: queued}. The completed job result retains the former payload: BridgeSpawnResult frozen dataclass mirroring the canonical service interface return.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report queued acceptance and the exact job_id, then inspect job.result. A completed operation whose status is failed reports a spawn failure, never success.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: macOS-side spawn of an MCP bridge subprocess.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: See the canonical service_interface entry; same error tokens.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: After successful dispatch, inspect the exact job.error before considering another invocation; an unreadable terminal write is not evidence that an effect did not occur. See the canonical service_interface entry.
